results.name: Svend Press Incline Bench
instructions: Lie on an incline bench with your feet flat on the floor and your back firmly against the bench. Hold a weight plate with both hands, pressing your palms against the flat sides of the plate at chest level with your fingers pointing up.
Engage your chest and press the weight plate straight out in front of you by extending your arms.
Squeeze your chest muscles as you press the plate outward until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly bring the plate back to your chest with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pressing through your chest, not your shoulders, to emphasize chest muscle activation.
Choose a weight that challenges you but allows you to maintain proper form.
Avoid locking your elbows completely at the top of the movement to keep tension on the chest muscles.
results.description: Svend Press Incline Bench is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Wide Push Ups Bodyweight
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your chest and lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 90-degree angle to your body.
Lower your chest until it is just above the floor.
Push through your hands to raise your body back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows at a 90-degree angle to your body to maximize chest and triceps engagement and reduce shoulder strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
Keep your head aligned with your spine to avoid straining your neck.
results.description: Wide Push Ups Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell behind your back with an overhand grip (palms facing backward), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended, and the barbell should rest against your glutes.
Flex your wrists to curl the barbell upward, bringing the barbell toward your forearms.
Hold the contraction at the top for a moment, squeezing your forearm muscles.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position by extending your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using your arms or shoulders to lift the barbell; focus on your wrist movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you curl the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury.
results.description: Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Wrist Curl Wide Legs
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet spread wide apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on the edge of the bench, allowing your wrists to hang over the edge.
Start with your wrists extended so the barbell is lowered as much as possible.
Curl the barbell upward by flexing your wrists, lifting the barbell as high as possible while keeping your forearms stationary on your thighs.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position by extending your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms stationary on your thighs to isolate your wrist flexors.
Avoid using your elbows to lift the barbell; focus on your wrist movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you curl the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
results.description: Barbell Wrist Curl Wide Legs is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Wrist Curl on Knees
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang over the edge.
Start with your wrists extended so the barbell is lowered as much as possible while maintaining control.
Curl the barbell upward by flexing your wrists, lifting the barbell as high as possible while keeping your forearms stationary on your thighs.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position by extending your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms stationary on your thighs to isolate your wrist flexors.
Avoid using your elbows to lift the barbell; focus on your wrist movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you curl the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
results.description: Barbell Wrist Curl on Knees is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Wrist Extension on Knees
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang over the edge.
Start with your wrists relaxed so the barbell hangs as much as possible.
Extend the barbell upward by extending your wrists, raising the barbell as far as possible while keeping your forearms stationary on your thighs.
Slowly bring the barbell back to the starting position by relaxing your wrists. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms stationary on your thighs to isolate your wrist extensors.
Avoid using your elbows to lift the barbell; focus on your wrist movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you extend the barbell down and inhaling as you curl it back up.
results.description: Barbell Wrist Extension on Knees is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Cable Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench facing the cable machine with a straight bar attached to the low pulley. Grasp the bar with both hands using an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands shoulder-width apart.
Rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists just beyond your knees, allowing the bar to hang down.
Curl the bar upwards by flexing your wrists, bringing the bar towards your forearms.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms stationary on your thighs throughout the exercise.
Focus on squeezing your forearms at the top of the movement.
Exhale as you curl the bar up and inhale as you lower it back down.
results.description: Cable Wrist Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Cable Wrist Extension
instructions: Stand sideways, facing away from a low cable pulley and hold the handle with one hand using an underhand grip. Bend your elbow to approximately 90 degrees and keep it tucked against your side with your forearm stationary.
Extend your hand at the wrist joint, moving your hand downward while keeping the rest of your arm still. Pause for 1 - 2 seconds.
Curl the weight by flexing at the wrist joint, bringing your hand upward. Pause for 1 - 2 seconds.
Slowly lower your hand back to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Keep your elbow tucked against your side throughout the exercise.
Move only at your wrist while keeping your forearm still.
Use a controlled range of motion without forcing your wrist beyond a comfortable position.
Inhale as you lower your hand and exhale as you raise it.
results.description: Cable Wrist Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Core.

results.name: Dumbbell Lying Pronation Rotation on Floor
instructions: Lie on your side on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. Support your head with the lower hand. Hold a dumbbell in the top hand with your elbow resting on your side, bent at a 90-degree angle, and your palm facing your head.
Slowly rotate your forearm, turning your palm down toward the knees while keeping your upper arm and elbow stationary.
Rotate your forearm back to the starting position with control, ensuring the movement is smooth and steady. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your upper arm and elbow stable throughout the exercise.
Avoid using excessive weight to ensure proper form and prevent strain on the wrist and elbow.
Focus on a slow and controlled rotation to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Dumbbell Lying Pronation Rotation on Floor is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell One Arm Reverse Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your forearm resting on your thigh, palm facing down, holding a dumbbell with an overhand grip (palm facing down).
Allow your wrist to extend downward so that the dumbbell hangs towards the floor, keeping your forearm stationary.
Curl the dumbbell upward as high as possible by flexing your wrist, focusing on engaging your forearm muscles.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your wrist. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your forearm stable and only move your wrist.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to avoid using momentum.
Focus on using your forearm muscles to lift the weight.
results.description: Dumbbell One Arm Reverse Wrist Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.
